Aniya: Quick share — I ran a small prototype of epilogue fusion that folds bias+rope into the fused-attn epilogue path. Short takeaway: 6–9% p99 drop for seq=1024 bs=1 on A100, throughput +8% for generation-only path.

Samir: Nice. Did you profile spills / register pressure? any differences in L2 traffic?

Aniya: Minimal extra regs in the kernel, but memory stores reduced since we write final output once instead of separate add/bias/rope passes. NVTX ranges attached.

Samir: Can you paste the exact command and perf output? want to reproduce.

Aniya: ```bash
./bench/run_infer.sh --model=gpt2-xl --seq_len 1024 --batch 1 --kernels=fused_attn_prototype --flags epilogue_fuse=1,bias_fuse=1,rope_fuse=1 --profile=nvprof --out=/tmp/epi-run
```
Perf excerpt (nvprof -> summary):
  kernel_time: fused_attn_epilogue 38.2ms (baseline 41.1ms)
  p99_latency: 45.6ms -> 42.3ms
  DRAM read: -12%

perf-bot: auto-bench: fused_epilogue_proto (A100) seq=1024 bs=1 throughput=110 tok/s (baseline 102), p99=42.3ms (baseline 46.5ms) 

Jordan: Curious about KV-cache / incremental decode behavior. Does fusing rope into epilogue change MVCC of cached keys? Any added writes when cache page hits are frequent?

Aniya: Good call. With the current implementation cache writes are identical for keys/values, but the final output path does fewer passes — so cold decode (first chunk) benefits most. We saw a slight regression (~2%) in streamed decode where we do many small steps because the fused epilogue is heavier on prologue setup for every decode step.

Lina: That aligns with microbenchmarks I ran: bs>1 shapes do better with epilogue fuse, but streaming bs=1 repeated calls pay setup cost. Also saw packed-QKV variant reduces L2 traffic but increases register pressure; on seq>2048 the packed path starts spilling.

Samir: Any numerical diffs? fusion sometimes touches precision (rope ordering, bias placement).

Aniya: Ran evals on our regression suite (100 prompts). Max token-level diff: <1e-6 after fp32 compute. But flagged one prompt where token ranking changed (likely borderline probability). We're adding a deterministic re-run to confirm.

Jordan: We should gate this behind a feature flag and a canary rollout (Dedicated first). Also add kernel-selection fallback: if seq>1500 or if L2 misses > threshold, pick non-packed epilogue.

Lina: Proposed heuristic: prefer epilogue_fuse for shapes where (seq*bs)>4096 and per-request tokens>256 but not for streaming small-step decodes. Add counters: epilogue_fuse_hits, epilogue_fuse_failures, kv_cache_page_writes.

Aniya: Plan: 1) add perf counters + nvtx markers, 2) add heuristics to kernel router, 3) run 24h canary on Dedicated pool, 4) if canary OK, enable for hosted read-only endpoints behind AB test.

Samir: If you see the streaming regression persist we can implement a lightweight small-step fast-path (no epilogue fusion) and then test traffic-split.

perf-bot: note: benchmark artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-dev/perf/epilogue_proto/1752504321/ (flamegraphs + nvprof) :thumbsup:

Aniya: Filing follow-ups: GH issue for kernel selection heuristics, perf job to sweep bs in {1,2,4,8} and seq in {512,1024,1536,2048}, and a test to catch token-ranking regressions. Will post links here once created. :rocket:
